definitions.explanation: Describes a state of physical disorder or lack of organization in a space or arrangement.

examples.japanese: {部屋|へや}が{乱雑|らんざつ}だ。
{机|つくえ}の{上|うえ}が{乱雑|らんざつ}に{散|ち}らかっている。
examples.english: The top of the desk is cluttered and messy.

examples.japanese: {書類|しょるい}が{乱雑|らんざつ}に{積|つ}み{上|あ}げられていて、{必要|ひつよう}なものが{見|み}つからない。
examples.english: Documents are piled up in a disorderly way, and I can't find what I need.

notes: Used for physical spaces and arrangements rather than abstract concepts. Common collocations include {乱雑|らんざつ}な{部屋|へや} (a messy room), {乱雑|らんざつ}に{置|お}く (to place haphazardly), and {乱雑|らんざつ}な{状態|じょうたい} (a disordered state). Compare with {散|ち}らかっている (scattered around, more colloquial) and {雑然|ざつぜん}とした (jumbled, similar formality level).
